About power stations in Kenya

A portable power station — often called a solar generator — is a rechargeable battery with a built-in inverter and normal AC sockets. It charges from a wall socket or from solar panels and runs your appliances silently when KPLC power goes off, with no fuel, fumes or installation. We stock 28 models from EcoFlow and BLUETTI, from KES 27,500 to KES 1,160,000.

Read moreShow less

Two numbers matter. Capacity, in watt-hours (Wh), is how much energy it stores; AC output, in watts (W), is how much it can power at the same time. For example, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 stores 1,024 Wh, so in a blackout it can run a 150 W fridge for approximately 6 hours (capacity × 0.85 ÷ watts), while its 1800W (Surge 3600W) AC output sets the largest load it can start.

27 of the 28 models use LiFePO4 (LFP) batteries, with ratings such as 3500+ cycles to 80%. LFP chemistry copes well with heat and keeps most of its capacity after thousands of charge cycles, which is why it suits daily use through frequent outages.

Under 500 Wh suits a Wi-Fi router, phones, a laptop and lights — for example the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh). 500 to 1,500 Wh covers lights, Wi-Fi, a TV and a fridge in a one- or two-bedroom home — see the EcoFlow DELTA 3. 1,500 to 4,000 Wh suits a family home through longer outages, like the BLUETTI AC200PL. Above 4,000 Wh, systems such as the BLUETTI Homestar 5 Solution back up a whole home.

Compare models side by side on our power station comparison page, read short answers in our backup power guide, and pair a station with our solar panels. Pay by M-Pesa, card or cash on delivery, with same-day delivery in Nairobi and delivery to all 47 counties with an eTIMS invoice.

Frequently asked questions

Which power station can run a fridge in Kenya?

A typical fridge uses about 150 W while running. Any of our stations with at least 1,000 Wh handles one through a normal outage: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1,024 Wh) runs a 150 W fridge for approximately 6 hours on its own. Check that the AC output covers the fridge's start-up surge; we can confirm on WhatsApp.

What is the difference between a power station and an inverter?

A home inverter system pairs a separate inverter with separate batteries and usually needs installation and wiring. A power station puts the battery, inverter, charger and sockets in one portable unit: you plug appliances straight into it and recharge it from the wall or solar panels, with no installation.

Can I charge a power station with solar panels?

Yes. 19 of our 28 models list a solar input; the EcoFlow DELTA 3, for example, accepts 500W Max (11-60V, 15A). Choose panels within that input limit, and message us on WhatsApp to confirm the right cable before you buy.

How long does a power station take to charge?

It depends on the model and the charger. From a wall socket the EcoFlow DELTA 3 is rated at 1500W Max, 0-80% in 60 mins. Solar charging time depends on panel wattage and sunshine, so larger panel arrays recharge faster. Each product page lists its own charging figures.

Can a power station back up my whole house?

Larger systems can. The biggest we stock, the BLUETTI EP2000 Solution (20kW Inverter + 29kWh – 51kWh Battery), stores 29,000 Wh. Whole-home backup depends on what you run at once, so send us your appliance list and we will size a system for you.

Is there a warranty, and how do I pay?

Every unit is genuine and covered by a 24-month warranty. Pay by M-Pesa, card or cash on delivery, with same-day delivery in Nairobi and delivery to all 47 counties with an eTIMS invoice.
